newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares down at noon on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares down at noon on correction.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were down slightly at midday on Friday due to a technical correction after the index surged 7.18 percent on Thursday, brokers said.
The decision of Shanghai Lujaizui Finance and Trade Zone Development not to propose any dividend or bonus share issues also had an impact on the market, they said.
The index fell 0.592 points or 0.72 percent to 81.800 points on volume of 28.218 million shares worth $13.606 million, compared with $9.68 million on Thursday.
"The market has been rising too fast, which triggered a large amount of profit-taking," one broker said. "Some institutions were seen liquidating their positions."
Unhappiness over Lujiazui's dividend plan accelerated the correction, brokers said, but added that the downward potential was limited due to continuing strong sentiment.
"The index will see support at 78 points," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 41 traded, with 22 down, two flat and 17 up.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the biggest loser on profit-taking, slipping $0.090 or 5.99 percent to $1.410 on volume of 355,000 million shares.
Shanghai Friendship & Overseas Chinese was the most actively traded stock on institutional buying, gaining $0.014 or 2.82 percent to $0.510 on volume of 3.2 million shares.
The Shanghai A share index was down on a continued correction, with investors concerned about the possibility of negative news energing over the weekend to cool down the market, brokers said.
The index fell 11.479 points or 0.83 percent to 1,373.309 points on volume of 296.2 million shares worth 3.7 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index slipped 23.815 points or 0.67 percent to 3,547.999 points.
Shanghai United Holding was the biggest loser on talk of unpromising results, slipping 0.55 yuan or 5.36 percent to 9.70 yuan on volume of 509,800 shares.
